title: Fenwick Energy deploy readiness jot
content:
Meeting capture: Fenwick Energy initial deploy-readiness call (quick personal jot)

Date: 2026-02-25
Attendees: Maya (Redwood SE), Arjun (Redwood infra), Sofia (Redwood PM), Tom L. (Fenwick infra lead), Priya K. (Fenwick security), Sam V. (Fenwick ML eng)

Quick summary:
- Fenwick is evaluating a private on-prem deployment (air-gapped option possible) for a field-worker assistant model.
- Primary constraints: strict data residency, HSM-backed keying, offline updates window, and low-latency at edge (subsidiary sites with limited bandwidth).
- They want a phased approach: PoC in their central DC -> pilot at 2 regional sites -> full roll in 6–9 months.

What they asked / requirements heard:
- Network / infra:
  - VPC-equivalent isolation in their DC; redundant NICs, support for NVMe-backed model cache on local hosts.
  - No outbound connections by default; control-plane sync only over scheduled windows (they may permit a jump-host for updates).
  - Want clear ops runbooks for air-gapped install + package verification checksum steps.

- Security & keys:
  - KMS/HSM integration mandatory. They use AWS CloudHSM in some regions but want vendor-agnostic design (we should support PKCS#11 or similar).
  - Audit log retention policy: 7 years for billing/usage metadata (internal compliance).
  - PII redaction at ingress (preferably configurable pipeline hooks) + ability to mark prompts as sensitive to skip telemetry collection.

- Performance & scale:
  - Typical request distribution: 70% short prompts (<128 tokens), 25% medium (512), 5% long (>2048).
  - Peak QPS target: 120 requests/s during day shift for central DC; regional sites 10–15 QPS.
  - Need 95th percentile latency <120ms for short prompts; can accept higher for long ones.
  - Throughput concerns + edge sites with 200ms last-mile—they want local caching of KV to avoid round-trip on every token.

- Model / eval expectations:
  - They want to start with a compact open model (we recommended quantized Llama-2.7B variant) and have a path to larger models if quality problems appear.
  - Must support deterministic rollbacks and canary traffic splitting for model updates.

Operational gotchas we flagged / they care about:
- Air-gapped ops means we must provide signed image bundles and an offline updater; packaging size matters (they will ship via physical media for remote sites).
- KV cache blowup for long-running sessions if session eviction policy not tuned — need explicit guidance for session length and memory sizing.
- GPU utilization at low QPS could make cost tricky; discuss batching vs reserved capacity tradeoffs.
- They run periodic forensic audits: need traceable request->model version mapping (token-level metadata must be exportable).
- Bandwidth-limited sites will require model variants locally (quantized) + fallback rules to central DC if model misses; we need robust routing policies and graceful degradation plans.

Open questions to follow up:
- Which HSM provider(s) at each target site? (Tom to confirm by 2026-03-04)
- Are there existing VM/container registries for air-gapped installs or do we ship OCI tarballs? (Priya to confirm)
- Exact retention window for request telemetry vs audit logs (Fenwick legal needs to sign off).
- Will they accept outbound-only telemetry over a jump-host every 12 hours, or must everything be fully offline?
- Expected RPS patterns for weekends/night shift (we only have weekday numbers)

Immediate next steps / owner notes (internal):
- Arjun: draft an air-gapped install runbook outline (include checksum verification, package signing, offline updater workflow). Target: 2026-03-05.
- Maya: prepare a sizing sketch for central DC + regional sites (GPU type suggestions, NVMe cache sizing, estimated costs for reserved capacity) — initial sketch by 2026-03-03.
- Sofia: open a concise proposal (1–2 pages) that lists recommended model variant, rollout timeline, SLAs, and optional managed-support add-ons; share with Fenwick by 2026-03-07.
- Follow-up demo: schedule a short remote demo showing on-prem installer + local caching in a sandbox. Tentative week of 2026-03-15.

Notes / rough numbers from call:
- Central DC: expecting ~120 short requests/s, avg token per request ~45 tokens -> ~5.4k tokens/s (useful for throughput math)
- Regional sites: 2 x sites initially, each ~12 QPS -> ~540 tokens/s each (estimate)
- Candidate infra: 8x A10G-ish GPU hosts for central DC (TBD), 1x A10G per regional site for pilot (budget constraint)

Potential risks / blockers:
- If HSM integration path requires custom engineering for PKCS#11 providers, timeline slips.
- Legal on telemetry retention could force us into an offline-only model which complicates monitoring/alerts.
- Physical media shipping for remote sites increases ops overhead and frequency of updates must be reduced (monthly vs weekly).

Brainstorm / options for tradeoffs (short):
- To meet latency SLO with fewer GPUs: aggressive quantization + local KV caching + model sharding per site. Quality risk but lowers cost.
- For telemetry constraints: provide on-demand secure export bundles that Fenwick can pull during accepted windows instead of continuous telemetry.
- Offer managed on-prem support for first 3 months to ease handoff; convert to a runbook + training package for long-term ops.

Loose todo/checklist (for my quick followups):
- [ ] Confirm HSM providers list (Tom)
- [ ] Package format decision (OCI vs tarball) + offline updater prototype
- [ ] Sizing doc v0 (Maya)
- [ ] 1–2 page proposal doc (Sofia)
- [ ] Book demo + internal dry-run before customer demo

Random notes / things to google before we prep proposal:
- Fenwick security policy reference (ask legal for redlined bits)
- Sample PKCS#11 integrations we've done for other customers (check PR history)
- Bandwidth-friendly model distribution best practices (delta updates for model weights)

End of jot — informal, will tidy before sending to Fenwick.
